alias-ref: error[krs::syntax::invalid-pattern-as]: `ref p @ pattern`: K's #as binds the matched term itself; remove `ref`
alias-inside-itself: error[krs::syntax::invalid-pattern-as]: identifier `p` is bound more than once in the same pattern: an alias cannot occur inside its own subpattern (E0416)
alias-remainder: error[krs::syntax::invalid-pattern-as]: `p @ ..`: a `..` remainder binds only inside a sequence, collection or cells! pattern
alias-in-result: error[krs::syntax::invalid-pattern-as]: `name @ pattern` binds only on a left-hand side (K's #as is LHS-only); refer to the name without `@` here
alias-whole-subject: error[krs::syntax::invalid-pattern-as]: `p @ pattern` cannot alias a whole rule subject: its root is the matched constructor or function; alias a subterm instead
or-unequal-binders: error[krs::syntax::invalid-pattern-or]: variable `x` is not bound in all alternatives
or-ambiguous: error[krs::analysis::ambiguous-or-pattern]: alternatives `Pair(x, y)` and `Pair(y, x)` of this or-pattern can match the same term with different bindings; K's #Or then is ambiguous (LLVM takes one, Haskell explores both). Make them disjoint or split the rule.
or-in-result: error[krs::syntax::invalid-pattern-or]: `|` is a pattern alternative; for Bool disjunction use bool::or or k::or_bool!
or-remainder: error[krs::syntax::invalid-pattern-or]: or-patterns combine terms, not remainders
matches-shadow: error[krs::analysis::invalid-matches]: `e` in k::matches! binds a new variable; it does not compare with the rule's `e`. Use int::eq/bool::eq, or write `_`
matches-guard: error[krs::syntax::invalid-matches]: K's :=K has no guard; conjoin a separate condition with bool::and
matches-std: error[krs::syntax::invalid-matches]: did you mean `k::matches!`? std's matches! tests a host value
matches-lhs: error[krs::syntax::invalid-matches]: `k::matches!` is a Bool test (K's :=K); it cannot appear on a left-hand side or inside a pattern
matches-alias-result: error[krs::expand::pattern-as-outside-lhs]: `p @ pattern` in a `k::matches!` pattern is allowed only in requires and ensures conditions: K rejects #as in a rule's right-hand side
matches-sort: error[krs::analysis::invalid-matches]: the pattern has sort `Color` and the subject has sort `Exp`, which share no subsort, so this test is always false
matches-claim: error[krs::expand::matches-outside-condition]: `k::matches!` is not supported in claims: the pinned native prover cannot resolve K's :=K in a claim; match the shape in the claim's subject instead
let-shape: error[krs::syntax::invalid-let]: a term block is `let pattern = term;`* followed by one result term (K's #let)
let-alias: error[krs::syntax::invalid-let]: `name @ pattern` cannot bind in a `let` pattern: K accepts #as only on a rule's left-hand side; bind the whole value with its own `let`
let-pattern: error[krs::syntax::invalid-let]: a `let` block (K's #let) is a term; it cannot appear on a left-hand side or inside a pattern
let-scope: error[E0599]: no variant, associated function, or constant named `__krs_variant_type_id_x` found for enum `ExpSyntax` in the current scope
let-sort: error[krs::analysis::invalid-let]: the pattern has sort `Bool` and the value has sort `Exp`, which share no subsort, so this `let` is always undefined
let-claim: error[krs::expand::let-outside-term]: `let` blocks are not supported in claims: the pinned native prover cannot resolve K's #let in a claim; bind the value in the claim's subject instead
context-remainder: error[krs::syntax::invalid-function-context]: a function context frames the rest of the configuration with an anonymous `..`
context-bound-rest: error[krs::syntax::invalid-function-context]: a function context frames the rest of the configuration with an anonymous `..`
context-on-rule: error[krs::syntax::invalid-function-context]: a configuration context belongs only on #[k::equation] (K's [[ ]] function context)
context-on-simplification: error[krs::syntax::invalid-function-context]: a configuration context belongs only on #[k::equation] (K's [[ ]] function context)
context-shape: error[krs::syntax::invalid-function-context]: a function context is a final `k::cells! { cell: .., .. }` parameter typed by the configuration struct
context-binders: error[krs::syntax::unsupported-rule-signature]: unsupported rule signature: typed term parameters must declare every term binder of the subject and function context, in first-occurrence order (hole binders included; `_`, remainders, HERE, instance labels and local binders excluded); a sentence with a function context declares every binder, here `n, b`
context-sort: error[krs::analysis::invalid-function-context]: the function-context binder `b` is declared `Bool`, but the cell `bar` holds `Int`
context-group: error[krs::analysis::invalid-function-context]: a function context reads leaf cells, not the whole nested cell `frame`; name the cells inside it
context-overlap: error[krs::analysis::overlapping-rule-heads]: rules `bump` and `read` can both apply to the same configuration at the same priority; K would take either one (nondeterminism). If that is intended, put both in one group with `#[k::rule(nondet = NAME)]`; otherwise refine a pattern, add disjoint `where` sorts or complementary requires guards, or order them with `owise` or `priority = N`.
